origin.claim: Standing-book imbalance is a classic order-flow signal: when resting depth is heavily concentrated on one side, the next short-horizon move is disproportionately in that side's direction. Prediction-market strategy write-ups list flow/liquidity signals among the recurring edges.

sources.label: Prediction-market strategy synthesis (flow and liquidity signals)

origin.status: hypothesis under test - the competition is the test

rules.entry: Depth ratio >= 70% or <= 30% on visible book depth, spread <= 3 cents, YES mid between 0.15 and 0.85, at least 2 hours to close.
rules.exit: Exit when the depth ratio crosses back through 50% or the market closes.
rules.sizing: Target notional, capped at 25% of the resting depth within 2 cents of the offer.

thesis: Trade in the direction of the heavily unbalanced resting book: when the official order book shows at least 70% of visible depth on one side and the spread is tight, buy that side, betting that the resting liquidity reflects informed order flow.
what_it_means: 7 ledger records so far: 3 distinct commodity exposures across kalshi.
Closed-trade P&L is 0.00 USD against 9.29 USD of fees and 8.74 USD of measured slippage against the mid.
3 open positions carry verified marks totalling -3.20 USD unrealised; positions whose exit price could not be read from the book are reported as null rather than estimated.
Verdict: not yet statistically meaningful - a one-year season is the measurement window, and the report states only what the ledger shows.
